video_title: Gracy Chen: This Will Trigger Bitcoin's Bull Market
gist: Bitget CEO Gracy Chen calls the post-rally market a 'monkey market' and a possible 2022 analog, argues crypto's value is now as TradFi infrastructure (stablecoins, tokenized equities/RWA), and lays out Bitget's Universal Exchange strategy and a 10%-penetration RWA vision for 2030.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's move from about $65k to $80k reflects fast sentiment change rather than changed fundamentals, since the Trump crypto conference, Clarity Act support and bond purchase were already-known information.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Rally is sentiment-driven and fragile; do not extrapolate it as a confirmed fundamental shift.
insights.quote: I don't think the foundation or the or the fundamentals changed that much

insights.claim: Chen calls the current market a 'monkey market', neither a typical bear nor bull market, because it jumps up and down; she advises against adding very high leverage.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Choppy two-way range argues for lower leverage and caution around chasing breakouts.
insights.quote: I will call it a monkey market because it just jumps up and down.

insights.claim: On the four-year cycle Chen sees 2026 as analogous to 2022, the start of a bear market rather than a bull start, and warns this implies another black swan event in the industry could push Bitcoin lower.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: A cycle-analog bearish tail risk from an exchange CEO; she explicitly hopes it is wrong.
insights.quote: 2026 is similar to 2022 in that sense.

insights.claim: Host Scott argues prices of RWAs and underlying assets lagged for a long time and may have needed a trigger, and that retail interest is returning: formerly uninterested people are messaging him and volumes are rising.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Anecdotal retail-return signal consistent with a sentiment turn.

insights.claim: Chen argues crypto lacks its own innovation but is becoming important infrastructure inside traditional finance; most L1/L2 chains have not survived or delivered utility, and GameFi, SocialFi and NFTs have not fulfilled their promises.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Favours exposure to financial-use-case assets over narrative web3 apps.
insights.quote: crypto is um is lack of its own innovation. uh however it is integrating to the traditional financial industry

insights.claim: Many chains valued above $1B have only single- or double-digit daily real developers, so they are effectively ghost chains.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Valuation versus developer activity is a screen for fragile L1 valuations.

insights.claim: Product-market fit is concentrated in trading platforms (Hyperliquid, Binance, Bitget) and in stablecoin cross-border payments, tokenized stocks and tokenized gold, silver and oil, driven by capital controls and hard-to-open broker accounts.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Stablecoin rails and RWA tokenization are where she expects the next few years of potential.

insights.claim: The World Bank estimate cited is that about 6% of cross-border transfers are lost to transaction and forex fees, which stablecoins can largely avoid.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Fee savings underpin the stablecoin remittance use case.
insights.quote: about 6% fees deducted due to transaction uh transaction fees or forex fees

insights.claim: Chen is doubtful that dead GameFi and social projects can be revived without strong product-market fit, and worries most about smaller projects lacking it.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Avoid small-cap projects with no demonstrable PMF.

insights.claim: Bitget supported xStocks tokenized equities from about Aug/Sep 2025 and by Q4 2025 accounted for 89% of total volume per data she cited; Bitget and Binance both launched RWA equity products in June 2026.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Offshore exchanges are capturing tokenized-equity volume ahead of traditional venues.
insights.quote: Q4 last year we even contributed to 89% of on those total volume.

insights.claim: Tokenized equity trading accelerated in 2026 once names like SpaceX were listed, pulling users to trade onchain stock versions instead of traditional exchanges; spot and equity perpetuals are both growing.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Listing high-profile stocks drives tokenized-equity adoption; watch equity perp volumes.

insights.claim: US regulators SEC and CFTC are discussing how to jointly regulate stock perpetuals, which straddle equity and derivatives jurisdiction.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Regulatory clarity on equity perps would open the US market segment.

insights.claim: Bitget research shows roughly 40-50% of its users hold both crypto and a traditional instrument such as equities or commodities, and Bitget serves more than 100 million users.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Crypto and TradFi holdings are converging within the same user base.

insights.claim: Chen's '10% vision' predicts tokenized penetration of traditional assets reaches about 10% by 2030 and 20-30% by 2035; today penetration is 0.5-1% in private credit and money market funds and about 0.01% in equities (a roughly $120T market with about $10B tokenized).
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Gives a quantified long-run TAM framing for RWA tokenization.
insights.quote: my 10% vision is that by 2030 all these penetration ratio should be around 10%

insights.claim: Chen sees collaborating with NYSE and Nasdaq on tokenization as the biggest challenge and opportunity for Bitget, and says it is in talks with both and other big exchanges.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Exchange-tokenization partnerships are a catalyst to watch.

insights.claim: Bitget positions as a Universal Exchange (similar to Coinbase's everything exchange), because DEX and CEX are merging; it concedes ETFs will win US institutions, family offices and endowments, and competes on trading tools, a unified trading account, AI tools and 24/7 service.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Exchanges are differentiating on tooling as Bitcoin exposure commoditizes via ETFs, DATs and brokers like Robinhood.

insights.claim: Listing assets early is only 'phase one' worth about 20% of value; the other 80% is trading experience.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Execution quality, not asset breadth, is her stated moat.
insights.quote: only does in my opinion 20% of the value or 20% of the work

insights.claim: Bitget spent 45 million USDT compensating users hurt by a violent altcoin price move on a Saturday about one to two weeks earlier.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Shows the cost of customer-protection policy for exchanges.

insights.claim: Trust-building measures: monthly proof of reserves since 2022, a protection fund above $400 million, no commingling lessons from FTX, and pursuing licenses by acquisition or application; Bitget gave Ethereum to Bybit after its $1.5B hack to cover short-term liquidity.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Industry-mutual-support and PoR are trust signals when comparing exchanges.

insights.claim: Bitget sees growing AI trading activity and moved from a chatbot (GetAgent) to execution tools; a stablecoin issuer told her it opens accounts for AI agents with a starting limit (for example $5,000) that rises as capability is proven, while Bitget still requires users to be KYC'd and responsible for their agents.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Agentic payments and trading are an emerging but still small crypto demand source.
insights.quote: there are more trading um activities from AI and I think this is a trend that nobody can ignore.

insights.claim: Adoption of any new technology takes time; Chen says only about 2% of the world has experienced good LLMs, and she believes everyone should own at least 0.1 Bitcoin to understand it.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Mass adoption is early-curve; a long runway but slow.

insights.claim: Chen says Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2035 (citing Cathie Wood and mining-cost estimates), conditional on global money supply growth, delivery of the RWA vision, quantum risk staying contained and more national reserve purchases.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Long-dated bull case with explicit conditions to monitor.
insights.quote: I do think it has that potential

insights.claim: Chen says the next few weeks before the US midterms are key: whether the Clarity Act passes and whether the US Treasury buys rather than just holds Bitcoin, though passage right before a midterm is hard and the issue is political rather than economic.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Low odds of a Clarity Act or reserve-buying catalyst before midterms; do not price it in.
insights.quote: it's hard to pass a a big act like clarity act

insights.claim: Germany's sale of Bitcoin holdings last year caused a dramatic intraday price move, so national reserves selling versus holding versus buying matters for price.
insights.speaker: Gracy Chen, Bitget CEO
insights.so_what: Government flows are a price risk and catalyst.
